title: South Korean Won Rises Slightly | Forex News 2025.10.10 (en)
content: The South Korean won strengthened slightly to approximately 1,420 per U.S. dollar on Friday, October 10, 2025, but remained near its weakest level in five months due to sustained strength in the U.S. dollar. The dollar’s continued strength throughout the week was driven by significant declines in the Japanese yen and euro. Domestically, market sentiment remained cautious following reports that over 470,000 South Korean companies failed to achieve net profitability in 2024, highlighting ongoing challenges in demand and fiscal revenue pressure. However, the outlook saw a modest improvement, supported by a fourth consecutive monthly increase in foreign reserves, which reached approximately USD 422 billion in September 2025, providing a limited buffer against external economic volatility.

title: 원/달러 환율, 넉 달 반 만에 1400원대... 달러강세·대미투자 불확실성 여파
content: The South Korean won/dollar exchange rate rose to the 1,400 won level for the first time in nearly five months, closing at 1,407.0 won on October 2, 2025, according to the Seoul foreign exchange market. The weekly average exchange rate was 1,403.33 won, marking the first time since May 12–16, 2025 (weekly average 1,405.86 won), when the rate had been above 1,400 won. The exchange rate remained above 1,400 won for four consecutive trading days during the week. This upward trend is attributed to dollar strength and uncertainty surrounding the $350 billion U.S.-Korea investment agreement. The U.S. dollar index rose from 96 in mid-September to 98 by late September, though it dipped to around 97 in the following week due to the U.S. government shutdown. Factors such as strong U.S. second-quarter economic growth and European security concerns contributed to the dollar’s strength. Ongoing deadlock in U.S.-Korea trade negotiations over investment mechanisms, combined with unclear currency swap arrangements, have increased pressure on the won. As no positive signals have yet come from the U.S. side, a reversal to won strength is expected to remain difficult in the near term.

title: [Why&Next]"격동의 4분기" 환율 전망 '1450원 vs 1350원' 갈리는 이유는
content: The exchange rate between the South Korean won and the U.S. dollar rose to an average of 1401.6 won per dollar in October 2025, the first time since April 2025 that it surpassed the 1400 level. This trend is primarily driven by ongoing uncertainty surrounding the $350 billion U.S. investment agreement between South Korea and the United States, which remains in deadlock. Experts are divided on the year-end exchange rate: some predict it could rise to 1450 won if the U.S. investment deal fails to reflect South Korea's position, while others believe it could fall to 1350–1360 won if a favorable agreement is reached at the APEC summit in Gyeongju. Key factors influencing the exchange rate include foreign investor sentiment, structural changes in the domestic foreign exchange market due to increased overseas stock investments by domestic 'Seohakgaimi' (online retail investors), and reduced export-related won conversion due to expanded overseas production by Korean firms. Additionally, potential U.S. government shutdowns and speculation about the next Fed chair could contribute to dollar weakness and won strength. Kim Yoo-ri of Asiae reported that the outcome of the APEC summit negotiations will be a critical turning point, with a positive resolution possibly pushing the exchange rate down to the 1350–1360 won range, while continued deadlock could keep the rate above 1400 won.

title: 치솟는 원/달러 환율... 넉 달 만에 1410원대 진입
content: The Korean won has surged against the U.S. dollar, reaching the 1,410‑won level for the first time in four months.  On September 26, 2025, the Seoul foreign‑exchange market quoted the KRW/USD rate at 1,413.70, up 4.70 won from the previous day and 8.4 won higher than the 1,409.0 won opening price.  The 1,412.1 won peak reached earlier in the session was the highest since May 15, when the rate also hit 1,412.1 won.  The rally follows a three‑day upward trend that began on September 24, breaking the psychological 1,400‑won resistance and later surpassing 1,410 won in after‑hours trading.  Analysts attribute the move to a decline in expectations of U.S. interest‑rate cuts and a strengthening of safe‑asset demand.  U.S. GDP for the second quarter rose 3.8 %—a surprise 0.5 percentage‑point lift over the preliminary 3.3 % estimate and the highest growth rate in seven quarters since the third quarter of 2023 (4.7 %).  Trade‑policy uncertainty also weighed on the won.  President Donald Trump confirmed that South Korea would invest $350 billion (about ₩490 trillion) in the U.S. under the trade agreement, saying, '그것은 선불(up front)'.  South Korean President Yoon Jae‑myung warned that a full‑cash payment of the $350 billion could trigger a crisis similar to the 1997 financial collapse, and proposed an unlimited currency‑swap plan to curb dollar outflows and a sharp rise in the KRW/USD rate.

title: 원·달러 환율, 1410원대 돌파
content: On September 26, 2025, the Korean won‑to‑US dollar exchange rate climbed above the 1,410‑won level, as shown at a currency exchange in Seoul’s Myeongdong. The article reports that the rate began the day at 1,409.0 won – an increase of 8.4 won from the previous day – and subsequently surpassed 1,410 won. The quoted figures in the article are '1,410원대', '1,409.0원', and '8.4원', confirming the rise in the currency pair.

title: 잭슨홀 디데이...원/달러 환율 3주 만에 1,400원 터치
content: The Korean won‑to‑US dollar exchange rate crossed the 1,400‑won mark for the first time in three weeks on August 22, 2025. At 9:11 am KST the rate was 1,399.5 won, having started the day at 1,400.0 won and peaking at 1,400.5 won. The rate had risen from 1,400.0 won the previous day and had not fallen below 1,378.5 won since August 14, remaining unchanged for six consecutive trading days. The dollar index increased 0.24 % to 98.601, reflecting a stronger dollar against six major currencies. Market participants are watching the upcoming Jackson Hole symposium, where Fed Chair Jerome Powell is expected to signal on monetary policy; a hint of an aggressive rate cut could weaken the dollar, while a muted message might leave the dollar resilient. KB Kookmin Bank researcher Lee Min‑hyuk said, '1,400원 부담이 있지만, 달러화 지수 상승과 나스닥 지수의 조정, 투자자의 위험회피심리 등이 원화에 부정적 영향을 미칠 것으로 예상된다' and added, '시장은 여전히 미국 물가 상승 경계와 연준 금리인하에 대한 확신이 부족한 것 같다'. The won‑to‑yen rate was 943.42 won per 100 yen, down 4.65 won from the previous close, while the yen‑to‑dollar rate was 148.385 yen, up 0.6 %.

title: 원-달러 환율 다시 1400원 넘어서
content: On September 25, 2025, the Korean won fell to 1,403.0 per U.S. dollar, a 5.5‑won increase from the previous trading day, marking the first time the exchange rate has crossed 1,400 won since August 1, 2023, when it was 1,401.4. The rise follows the U.S. Federal Reserve's 0.25‑percentage‑point rate cut on September 17 and its cautious stance on further cuts, which has strengthened the dollar. The dollar index climbed from 96.22 on September 17 to 97.22 on September 24. During the same period, the Japanese yen weakened against the dollar, moving from the 146‑yen range to the high‑148‑yen range, reflecting a 1‑yen depreciation. The article notes that Japanese opposition parties, supporting the ruling party's next‑prime‑minister candidates, are pushing for '재정 지출 확대', a stance that has contributed to the yen's sharper decline.

title: [포토] 원·달러 환율 1420원 돌파...5개월 만에 '최고'
content: The South Korean won/dollar exchange rate surged to 1,423.0 won on October 10, 2025, marking its highest level in five months, according to a monitor at the Hana Bank dealing room in Seoul’s Jung-gu district. The rate rose by 23.0 won from the previous trading day. On the same day, the KOSPI index opened 48.90 points (1.38%) higher at 3,598.11, while the KOSDAQ index rose 4.61 points (0.54%) to 858.86. The increase in the exchange rate occurred after a long holiday period, signaling renewed market volatility.

title: South Korean Won Rises on Fed Rate Cut Bets | Forex News 2025.10.15...
content: The South Korean won strengthened to approximately 1,426 per dollar on October 15, 2025, recovering from prior losses as the U.S. dollar weakened amid rising market expectations of further Federal Reserve monetary easing. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell stated on October 14, 2025, that employment and inflation projections have remained largely stable since the Fed's first rate cut in September 2025. Domestically, the won gained support from the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) revised 2025 growth forecast for South Korea, which was increased to 0.9 percent—up 0.1 percentage point from the July estimate—due to less severe-than-expected impacts from U.S. tariff policies.

title: 넉 달 만에 1410원 돌파한 환율... 하루 만에 10원 넘게 폭등
content:
The Korean won‑dollar exchange rate surpassed 1,410 won for the first time in four months, closing at 1,412.4 won on September 26, 2025 – an 11.8‑won rise from the previous day.  The 1,410‑won level was last seen on May 15, 2025 at 1,412.1 won.

The rally is attributed mainly to strong U.S. economic data.  The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis released the revised second‑quarter GDP growth rate on September 25, reporting a 3.8 % annualized increase – 0.5 percentage points higher than the preliminary 3.3 % and the highest since the third quarter of 2023 (4.7 %).  The dollar index (DXY) was 98.38 at 4:13 p.m. local time, up 0.74 % from a week earlier and breaking the 98‑level.

Expectations for a Fed rate cut have weakened.  The CME FedWatch tool showed that the probability of a rate freeze at the next FOMC meeting on October 26 was 12.3 %, up 6.2 percentage points from 8.1 % the day before.

Domestic uncertainty also fed the yen’s rise.  A dispute over a 350 billion‑dollar Korean‑U.S. investment fund has stalled trade talks; former U.S. President Donald Trump described the fund as “pre‑paid,” heightening market concerns.  As a result, foreign investors sold 832.2 billion won of Korean stocks, and the KOSPI fell 85.06 points (2.45 %) to 3,386.05.

Economist Woo Jae‑hyun of NH Futures noted, ‘지난주 환율 상승을 주도했던 대미투자 관련 불확실성에 더해, 이번 주는 미국의 견조한 펀더멘털에 따른 달러화 강세도 나타나며 환율 상승 압력이 확대됐다’ and added, ‘단기적으로 환율 상단을 1400원에서 1420원으로 상향 조정한다.’
